en.content:
As Hong Kong marks the 29th anniversary of the Handover, the government’s decision to roll out city-wide offers spanning transport, arts, leisure and food is more than a routine celebration. It is also a public signal about priorities: to stitch everyday life back into the commemorative moment, and to reassure residents that policy attention is not confined to the realm of security or administration. In a period marked by geopolitical tension and economic uncertainty, modest “near-at-hand” benefits can function as social glue—reminding people that civic life is meant to feel tangible, not merely symbolic.

At the same time, the effectiveness of freebies will inevitably depend on perception. Some residents may welcome the easing of costs and the opening of more cultural and recreational access; others may ask whether such promotions substitute for harder work—addressing housing pressure, youth employment and livelihood affordability. A celebration that reaches into daily spending is politically safe, but it risks being judged by the yardstick of lasting improvements rather than temporary relief. The government would do well to treat these initiatives as complements, not alternatives, to structural policies.

More interestingly, the anniversary theme is taking on a “normalisation” character. By pairing commemorative messaging with public-facing consumption and movement, authorities appear to be steering attention toward routine stability—an implicit answer to concerns that Hong Kong is still navigating an identity and future under constraints beyond its immediate control. This approach aligns with the broader official narrative of maintaining order and improving governance while promoting social cohesion. If the city can sustain a sense of shared participation—through arts, community events and orderly transport arrangements—the celebration becomes a quiet endorsement of confidence in the “one country, two systems” framework.

Still, inclusiveness matters. The government’s rollout should be evaluated not only by how widely it is advertised, but by whether it serves residents across districts and income levels without creating new friction or bottlenecks. In particular, events connected to transport and popular venues should be designed with accessibility in mind, so the benefits are felt by families, the elderly and commuters rather than concentrated among those who are already better positioned to take advantage. In that sense, the July 1 offers are best read as an opportunity for governance to demonstrate competence in everyday details—the kind of service that, over time, can build trust more reliably than slogans alone.
en.topic_title: City-wide arts, leisure, F&B and transport offers and freebies unveiled for July 1 Handover anniversary

zh.content:
香港政府今次提出「讓特首可認定某些刑事行為屬於國家安全罪行」嘅立法方向，表面係要「使法例更清晰」，但社會最關心其實唔係口號，而係權力點樣落地、證明門檻幾高，以及司法程序仲有冇足夠空間去制衡。國安框架本來就容易因定義延展而引發疑慮；一旦由行政主導「先行貼標籤」，即使最終交由法院審理，個標籤本身都可能先行影響輿論、調查策略同檢控取向，形成「先確定性」而非「後由證據證明」。

不過，立法同樣唔可以只用情緒對立思維去否定。真正應該被追問嘅係：立法文本會否清楚界定特首可作認定嘅範圍，並列明可依循嘅客觀標準？又會唔會設有緊密嘅司法覆核路徑，例如保證被影響人士可以及時提出程序性挑戰、要求出示足夠理據？如果只係把「含糊」包裝成「清晰」，但冇提高程序透明度同可被挑戰性，所謂「清楚」就可能只係對執行者而言更好操作，對市民而言則更難預知風險。

同時，今日香港亦面對多重壓力：一方面政府宣稱維持社會穩定，透過公共服務、福利同消費活動去凝聚節慶氣氛；另一方面，個別案件亦顯示「言論」同「政治」之間嘅界線仍然引人擔心。喺呢種氣氛下，國安認定權一旦擴張，就更需要配套去確保「必要性」同「比例性」。要有制度去防止執法由「保護安全」滑向「管理風險」；否則再強調「法例清楚」，都未必能夠補足市民對公平程序同權利保障嘅基本要求。

我嘅立場係：支持政府在法律上作出合理釐清，但反對任何形式嘅權力「擴大性」、或用行政認定取代法庭對事實同罪責嘅判斷。若政府真係想做到「使法例更清晰」，就應該公開更細嘅操作準則、提供更可追溯嘅理據、並把司法覆核與保障措施寫得更實、更硬。國家安全可以是社會需要，但香港嘅管治方式必須繼續以法治為核心；清晰唔應該只係方便執行，而係要令市民知道界線、亦知道自己可以點樣爭取救濟。
zh.topic_title: ‘Make law clear’: John Lee defends plan to give Hong Kong leader power to certify criminal acts as nat. sec offences
